result.title: Program Distillation: Transferring LLM Capability from System 2 to System 0
result.summary: Recent studies leverage large language models (LLMs) to construct executable programs through environment interaction, feedback analysis, and code revision. However, prior work has mainly treated LLMs as optimizers, overlooking their ability to transfer knowledge across system levels. We propose Program Distillation (PD), a framework that formalizes the transfer of abilities from System 2 to System 0. During learning, the LLM provides task knowledge and draft strategies; at deployment, a student program executes the resulting policy. We show that this approach can improve performance while reducing inference time. We introduce PDBench, a benchmark comprising 27 discrete- and continuous-control tasks with fixed initial policies, and PDMetaHarness, a model-harness-independent meta-system for monitoring and guiding the learning process. The strongest model achieves a normalized mean score of 0.728, surpassing PPO (0.656) and Jev-like decision models (0.239), while running exclusively on CPUs and reducing inference costs. Our analysis shows that performance is largely driven by the first breakthrough during learning, and structural modifications have a slightly lower success rate than parameter modifications but typically yield larger gains. We further introduce style distillation, which enables interpretable stylistic control over the learning process. Overall, we present an analytical framework for PD and demonstrate its practical viability.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Program Distillation，把 LLM 的任务知识与策略蒸馏成部署时执行的学生程序，并构建 PDBench 与 PDMetaHarness 在离散和连续控制任务上评估性能与推理成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将 System 2 显式推理迁移为快速 System 0 策略，可能为 LVR 把多步推理压缩进 latent 或轻量执行状态提供训练监督与成本对照线索，但材料未涉及视觉多模态状态，迁移可行性有待核查。
